notes: Approved gouache harbour painting whose rust roofs and ochre hillside collapse to one value along the ridge plus a stray teal water line; the wordmark surviving only as tapering hand paint on a shed; the shop's continuous-flow act card PDF; a 14-row acts CSV with 3 blank portraits, a double-booking, an ampersand, an accent and one overlong name; 11 self-shot portraits (3 tiny, 2 the same act); and a clean shop note.

assets.prompt: A flat scan of an approved folk-festival illustration painted in gouache and watercolour on board, upright portrait. Scene: a working fishing harbour at late afternoon, a long weathered timber quay shed across the middle ground, a crowd of small painted figures gathered on the quay, fishing boats at the water, and rolling hills rising behind the town. Painterly, folk-art screenprint-poster feel but rendered as an actual painting with real brush and wash. CRITICAL COLOUR STRUCTURE, reproduce exactly: the sky is a graded harbour-blue wash (#2F5A6E) carrying many subtle intermediate values rather than one flat field; the shed and boathouse ROOFS are painted rust red (#B5502F); the HILLSIDE directly behind and above those roofs is painted hill ochre (#C69A46); along the RIDGE where the rust roofs meet the ochre hill the two colours are mixed down to almost exactly the same mid tone so the roofline and the hill edge nearly disappear into each other (very low contrast at that seam). Figures, boat hulls, window frames, ropes and outlines are painted in deep near-black ink (#22282B). The unpainted board shows through as a warm kraft-paper tone (#E4D6BC) in the sky gaps and margins, used as a colour. Along the very bottom, in the water lapping the quay, there is a single thin painted quay-teal line (#3E8C86) that appears nowhere else in the painting and reads as if it could be part of the sky. Rich washes, dry-brush texture, no visible logo, no readable lettering.
assets.defect_engineered: ridge value-collapse (rust roofs and ochre hill run to one value at the seam) + the fifth colour, a lone thin teal water line, plus tonal washes with hundreds of intermediate values in sky and water for the halftone-screen checkpoint

assets.prompt: Handheld daylight photograph shot from the quay of the long side wall of a weathered timber harbour shed, grey silvered vertical planking, late afternoon. Hand-painted across the boards in thick chipped off-white paint is the single word WHARFSIDE in tall rough hand-lettered capitals, the festival's own painted sign since 2006. The wall is NOT square to the camera: it recedes left to right so the lettering visibly TAPERS, larger and taller at the near left end and smaller toward the far right. The last three letters (I D E) run into the deep shadow of the roof overhang where the pale paint and the weathered grey timber sit very close in value and are hard to separate. The paint is broken and flaked at stroke level over the coarse grain (disjoint strokes, gaps in every letter). The enclosed counters of the round letters (the bowl of the R, the bowl of the D, the triangle of the A) are painted open. No other signage, no people. Realistic snapshot, slight barrel distortion, not a studio shot.
assets.defect_engineered: wordmark survives only as photographed paint on timber: paint-vs-plank selection trap, disjoint flaked strokes that defeat a subject knockout, enclosed counters that cannot be punched by background removal, left-to-right camera taper, and last three letters lost in roof-overhang shadow

LAYOUT SPEC for wharfside_nightcard_2025.pdf — render as a genuine single-page press PDF from a full layout engine with embedded font subsets (NOT a thin hand-authored PDF). Trim 105 x 148 mm (A6 portrait), NO bleed and no crop marks. One act per card; this is last year's card carrying last year's opening act.

CRITICAL STRUCTURE (this is the planted trap, author it exactly): the four visible blocks below must be set as ONE single continuous text flow in ONE text frame (a single story with line breaks between the blocks), NOT four separate frames. The portrait must be DRAWN as a filled/stroked rectangle placeholder with a painted grey fill, NOT a placed image frame — there is to be no graphic/image frame anywhere in the document. The page must therefore convert to exactly one TextFrame and zero graphic frames.

VISIBLE BLOCKS (top to bottom, all inside the one story):
  Block 1 — festival line, small caps: WHARFSIDE FOLK FESTIVAL — NINETEENTH YEAR
  Block 2 — portrait panel: a plain warm-grey drawn rectangle roughly 60 x 72 mm centred, with the caption line under it: 'photo: supplied by the act'
  Block 3 — act name, large display: The Fen Larks
  Block 4 — details, three lines: Stage: Quay Stage / Night: Friday / Set: 7.00 pm

Field labels the merge will later target (as they read in the story): ACT NAME, STAGE, NIGHT, SET TIME. Colours: deep ink (#22282B) type on kraft-paper (#E4D6BC) ground. Type set for flat opaque screen ink, generous margins.

assets.content:
QUAYSIDE HAND PRESS — notes for the Wharfside twentieth-year run (from Del & Marina, two streets up)

How we print. Everything is pulled by hand on the flatbed. We run FOUR inks plus the colour of the paper. The paper is one of your colours, so leave it working, do not flood it. On the shirt we can only give you TWO inks, no paper showing through as a colour because the cloth is the ground.

Stock.
- Poster: 300gsm uncoated kraft-toned board, natural oatmeal (about #E4D6BC). This is the big one for the shed and shop windows. True printed size 500 x 700 mm, portrait.
- Handbill: same natural oatmeal stock at 170gsm, trimmed to A5, 148 x 210 mm portrait. Same design as the poster, not a new one.
- Shirt: natural undyed cotton, print area about 300 mm wide across the chest.

Inks we are mixing for you: harbour blue, rust red, hill ochre, deep ink. If you need a fifth you have to drop one, we cannot run five plus the paper.

Registration. Hand pulled, so give us corner crop marks on all four corners AND one centre cross target, common to every plate so we can line them up. Expect 1 to 1.5 mm of slop between plates, so trap anywhere two solids butt: overlap the lighter ink under the darker by about 1 pt. Tell us on the spec which plate traps under which.

Line and tone. Minimum positive line 1.5 pt (about 0.5 mm). Minimum reversed (paper knocked out of ink) 2 pt or it fills in. We can only hold a COARSE dot by eye, roughly 20 to 25 lines to the inch, no fine screens and no process rosettes. Pick the coarseness against the size the thing actually prints at, and tell us the number. A screen that looks right on the poster will plug on the handbill if you do not think about it.

Act cards. Same A6-ish card as last year, one act per card, run on the small press. Fourteen this year.

Deadline. Films / positives in our hands by 15 August. Anything after that and the twentieth year prints late.
assets.defect_engineered: none (clean support asset: the shop's true constraints — four inks plus paper, two-ink shirt, coarse-dot-only halftone, 1.5pt min line, poster 500x700mm vs handbill A5 for the 3.4x reduction checkpoint, registration/trap practice, film deadline)
